messages:
Emma: quick heads-up — ran a short experiment separating 'seed-fill' (init tokens) from streaming generation on a single p4 node. dumping notes here.
bench-bot: run started 1702504300, 10k requests, model=open-gpt-large-8k-quant, config snapshot uploaded.
Raj: nice. what's the kernel mix look like? did the selector prefer matmul-vec for seed-fill?
Emma: initial run used stock kernel mapping. after we split queues: seed-fill showed ~60% matmul-vec kernels, decode/stream stuck to cublas-heavy path (~85%).
Frank: did you observe any KV cache churn — separating should change priming behavior.
Emma: KV hit rate for seed queue jumped 72% -> 93% (we primed prefixes). decode queue had intermittent misses when streams interleaved.
Olivia: did you try per-queue token budgets? seems like an obvious knob.
Emma: yes. token_budget: seed=48, stream=12. handshake latency dropped for seed (p50 18ms -> 12ms) but decode p50 moved 28ms -> 32ms (more small microbatches).
Raj: throughput vs latency trade. any tail regressions?
Emma: decode p99 jumped 290ms -> 410ms on the first run. root cause looks like frequent kernel switches when decode microbatches coalesce and trigger cublas path. kernel swap cost shows up on tail.
Frank: can we bias the kernel selector per-queue? e.g., tag decode batches with a streaming hint to prefer low-overhead kernels.
Emma: trying a quick scheduler tweak, config snippet attached below.
Emma: ```
# scheduler tweak for probe
queues:
  seed:
    token_budget: 48
    kernel_hint: "vector"
  stream:
    token_budget: 12
    kernel_hint: "streaming"
```
Olivia: Emma — can you add a small jitter to batch windows (0-5ms) to avoid synchronized churn? that helped earlier experiments.
Emma: added a microbenchmark: median kernel-swap cost = 4.2ms, 95th = 9.1ms — that lines up with the p99 spike.
bench-bot: job finished. artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/1702504321-seedfill-stream/ ; flamegraph: s3://redwood-perf/1702504321-seedfill-stream/flame.svg
Raj: next steps: 1) run with per-queue kernel_hint 2) enable 0-5ms jitter on stream queue 3) nudge decode token_budget up (try 16) 4) run multi-node to validate KV priming at scale.
Olivia: +1 on multi-node — priming benefits might dilute when requests are sharded across GPUs.
Emma: I'll kick off a 50k job with kernel hints + jitter + decode token_budget=16. will post artifacts and a short flamegraph. :rocket:
